subject: A Nimble Function for a Lookup Table

messages.author: 1c0200a388f5febd
messages.subject: A Nimble Function for a Lookup Table
parts:
Dear Nimble Users,

I'm working on building a model where one of the parameters (I'm calling it R) is a deterministic function of other model parameters, but this function requires numerical integration.  Since we can't call out to other R packages to do the numerical integration in a nimble function yet, I was thinking of creating a lookup table for R instead.  However, I understand that indexing via R's boolean vectors (e.g. x[x>5]) is not accessible in the Nimble language.  Do you have any ideas how I might write a Nimble function to use a lookup table?

An Example Lookup Table:
R   param1  param2
3         1            1
4         1            2
...

So I want something like:
"lookupR(1,1)" returns "table[ table[,2]==1 & table[,3]==1 , 1 ]"

messages.subject: Re: A Nimble Function for a Lookup Table
parts:
Yes!  This is VERY helpful - thank you :)

The other problem I'm running into is that I really want to use the round() function in my Nimble lookup table function, so that, for example

lookupR( 1.12, 0.98 ) returns the same as lookupR( 1, 1 )

I'm hoping to be able to pass in doubles, but only have a table for integer values.

I tried using round() in my Nimble function and in my BUGS model code with no luck.  So I started trying to build a (very) rudimentary round function (below), but I think I'm running into trouble trying to multiply an integer by a double (maybe?), as I get a setSizes error when I compile this function.  Any ideas?  Thanks again for all your help!!

roundNim <- nimbleFunction(

  run = function( x = double(0) ){

  returnType(double(0))

  absx <- abs(x)

low <- as.integer(absx)

high <- as.integer(absx+1)

if ( (absx-low) < 0.50 ){

return(sign(x)*low) } else {

return(sign(x)*high) }

})

messages.author: bebd85531a67ef86
messages.subject: Re: A Nimble Function for a Lookup Table
parts:
Your welcome :0)

How about the following for the round problem. "as.integer" and "sign" were both problematic.  

roundNim <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0) ){
      returnType(double(0))
      absx <- abs(x)
      low  <- floor(absx)   ## as.integer(absx) 
      high <- ceiling(absx) ## as.integer(absx + 1)

out <- low * (-1)^(x < 0)
      } else {
          out <- high * (-1)^(x < 0)
      }
      return(out)
  }
)

c_roundNim <- compileNimble(roundNim)

c_roundNim(0.56)  ## 1
c_roundNim(0.46)  ## 0
c_roundNim(-0.56) ## -1
c_roundNim(-0.46) ## 0

c_roundNim(1.5)  ## 2 
c_roundNim(0.5)  ## 1 
c_roundNim(-0.5) ## -1 
c_roundNim(-1.5) ## -2

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: A Nimble Function for a Lookup Table
parts:
Whoops, I meant to respond to this earlier.

We have a round() function in the NIMBLE DSL (i.e., allowed in run
code in a nimbleFunction). Here's a simple example of using it within
a nimbleFunction:

f = nimbleFunction(run=function(x = double(0)) {
returnType(double(0))
y = round(x)
return(y)
})

It sounds like you already tried our round() though? If so, what
errors did you run into?
